slides.beatName: Orientation: What we’ll learn and why it matters
slides.slideTitle: A benchmark you run once tells you nothing; hyperfine runs it until the numbers settle
Hyperfine runs every command at least 10 times and aims for about 3 seconds of measurement

slides.subtitle: run.sh
slides.slideTitle: Hyperfine picks the run count for you
Warmup runs and prepare commands decide whether you measure a warm cache or a cold one

keyBullets: Warm: --warmup 3 runs the command three times before measuring
Cold: --prepare clears the page cache before each run

slides.subtitle: cache.sh
keyBullets:
hyperfine -S --warmup 3 'grep -R TODO *'
hyperfine -S --prepare 'sync; echo 3 | sudo tee /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches' 'grep -R TODO *'

slides.slideTitle: Below 5 ms, a shell's startup is more noise than your command: run it without one

keyBullets: Use -S for pipes, redirections, and wildcards
With a shell, hyperfine subtracts its startup time
Below 5 ms, that correction is noise of its own
